limits: 1358 stock/C sequence comparisons cover complete/retried messages, all255 nonzero first counters, allocation failures, callback words/results, CRC rejection and live backend mutation scenarios. Actual C memmove/memcpy and CRC bodies execute. Ten sequences use the actual C fragment sender and then the actual C receiver; generated frames also match an independent polynomial implementation. Heap allocation/free, logging and final transmit/receive callbacks are modeled. The actual receive queue, ingress consumer, RTOS and physical radio are not executed here; their existing objects remain unchanged.

Thirteen C-only safety scenarios are intentionally not asserted equal to unsafe stock execution. The native ACK-table overwrite is reproduced only in emulated SRAM. No firmware or device memory is changed.

Callbacks are synchronous borrowed-buffer interfaces and their results do not affect the native completion return. One global stream is preserved; connection isolation, reentrancy and asynchronous concurrency are not established. Incidental scratch registers/private stack addresses are excluded; callee-saved integer/FP registers, masks, SP, state, heap/scratch content, emitted records and guards are checked. Source execution into stock code is rejected.
